title: Give Thanks
subtitle: The Blessings We Stop Noticing
tagline: A blessing doesn’t become ordinary because it happens every day.
headline: The Blessings We Stop Noticing
seo_title: Taking Blessings for Granted: The Ten Lepers in Luke 17
seo_description: Ten men were healed. One came back to say thank you. A Thanksgiving devotional for men on taking blessings for granted and the grace we stop seeing.
og_image_alt: The Blessings We Stop Noticing: A blessing doesn’t become ordinary because it happens every day. TheWrkShop.

scriptures.text: One of them, when he saw he was healed, came back, praising God in a loud voice. He threw himself at Jesus’ feet and thanked him—and he was a Samaritan.
Jesus asked, “Were not all ten cleansed? Where are the other nine? Has no one returned to give praise to God except this foreigner?” Then he said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well.”

blocks.text: Jesus heals ten men with leprosy.
All ten are healed.
Only one comes back.
And Luke wants you to notice who it is.
HE WAS A SAMARITAN.
The outsider. The one nobody expected to know how to respond to God.
Jesus even calls him “this foreigner.”
The nine who belonged kept walking.
The one who didn’t belong turned around.
We don’t know why the nine kept going.
We know the one who came back.
He recognized that something extraordinary had happened, and he refused to move on without thanking the One who did it.
“I’LL BE GRATEFUL WHEN SOMETHING BIG HAPPENS.”
We often save gratitude for extraordinary moments.
But what about the ordinary?
These gifts can become so familiar that we stop noticing them.
The problem is not always open ingratitude.
Sometimes it is inattention.
We become consumed by what is missing.
Our attention becomes organized around what we lack.
And because attention shapes affection, we begin experiencing our lives mostly through what’s missing.
WHAT WE KEEP NOTICING SHAPES WHAT WE BELIEVE OUR LIVES ARE ABOUT.
ALL TEN WERE HEALED. ONLY ONE HEARD, “YOUR FAITH HAS MADE YOU WELL.”
This is what taking blessings for granted looks like: the gift stays, and the gratitude fades.
The nine received a miracle.
The one who returned received something more: an encounter with the One who gave it.
Gratitude doesn’t just acknowledge the gift.
It brings us back to the Giver.
And gratitude is not denial of difficulty. It is recognition of grace within reality.
It doesn’t require pretending everything is good.
It invites us to acknowledge the good God has given, even while other things remain unresolved.

items: What blessing has become so familiar that I barely notice it?
What answered prayer have I stopped remembering?
What person do I now take for granted?
Have my unmet desires become louder than my received gifts?
What would change if I gave as much attention to grace as I give to problems?

blocks.text: Before asking God for anything today, name five specific gifts.
Then look for one chance to say thank you to another person.
A blessing doesn’t become ordinary because it happens every day.

Father, open my eyes to the gifts I have stopped noticing. Forgive me for letting familiarity dull my wonder. Help me recognize Your goodness in extraordinary moments and ordinary days. Teach me to turn around and come back with thanksgiving. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
The nine kept walking. The one turned around.
Familiarity can make grace feel invisible.
Gratitude doesn’t just acknowledge the gift. It brings us back to the Giver.
What we notice shapes what we appreciate.
A blessing doesn’t become ordinary because it happens every day.
